pullRequest.title: Place the level 0 scenery of a region as objects
pullRequest.body:
Closes #49

Spec: `spec/35-draynor-region-import.md` (part 6).

The import of `48_50` now fills `Scenery 48_50` with 1,894 objects for its 1,874 level 0 placements. 185 meshes are shared and 1,154 are own meshes. No placement shows nothing.

- Added `blender/region_scenery.py`. Placements with the same models, recolours and retextures share one mesh, and the object holds the position, turn and scale (the mirror is a scale of -1 on y). A placement that `own_vertices` bends gets its own mesh from its moved vertices, and its object holds only the position. The meshes come from `model_to_object`, with the textures from the decoded images.
- Updated `blender/region_import.py`. It reads the landscape, the locs and the models before it makes anything, places the scenery and returns the counts that the report of #50 needs.
- Added `read_locs` to `formats/loc_definition.py`. It also reads the locs that the impostors name.
- The fixture cache gets the loc group and an empty keys folder. The tests that run without the real cache then import no scenery, because the fixtures hold no loc models.

The owner's choices are in the [Decisions comment on #49](https://github.com/julian-perge/blender-addon-rs317-667mqo-makeup/issues/49#issuecomment-6888052393).

Guesses and choices of my own:
- A loc or a model that the cache lacks stops the import with a message, the same as a missing texture (#47).
- Each mesh gets its own materials, so `48_50` makes 3,172 materials. Sharing them is left for later.
- Several models of one loc are joined with `appearance.merge`, which gives an old-format model. A recolour of 127 on such a model would be refused with the old-format message. No loc of `48_50` does this.
- Two placements of the same loc on one tile get the same object name, and Blender numbers the second.
- The scenery tests need the real cache. The fixtures hold no loc models.

Run time and memory of the import of `48_50` (spec, guess 5): 5.6 seconds, and the peak memory of Blender went from 240 MB to 524 MB. The terrain alone took ~1 second.

Verification:

```bash
RSPS_SNAPSHOT_430_CACHE=<path to cache> BLENDER_USER_RESOURCES="$PWD/.blender-test-profile" scripts/test-blender.sh tests/blender/test_region_import.py
prek run --all-files
```

Both pass (911 Blender tests), and the pyrefly baseline has no new entry.

nodes.title: The region import places the level 0 scenery as objects
nodes.body:
Parent: #35
Spec: `spec/35-draynor-region-import.md` (part 6, Blender objects and meshes)

## What to build

The region import puts the level 0 placements in the child collection of the scenery.

- The import reads the landscape, and uses the placements on level 0 in the order of the file. A placement that shows nothing makes no object, and the import counts it.
- One Blender object per placement that shows a model. Placements with the same loc model, recolours and retextures share one mesh. The mesh is made with `model_to_object`, so it keeps the look of model import and has no baked loc light. Scale, rotation and position stay on the object.
- A placement that needs its own mesh (contoured on uneven ground, or a transform that Blender cannot hold) gets a mesh that holds the vertices after the transform and the contour. Its object holds only the position.
- An animated loc shows its model with no animation. An impostor shows the loc for value 0.
- Names: scenery objects `Loc <id> at <x>_<y>`, shared meshes `Loc <id>` with a suffix for recolours and retextures.
- Textures come from the decoded images, not from the texture folder.
- The modules are `blender/region_scenery.py`, and the changes to `blender/region_import.py`. The operator keeps the numbers that the report needs: placements made, shared meshes, own meshes, placements that showed nothing.
- Run time and memory: record the run time of the import in the pull request (spec, guess 5).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The import of `48_50` makes one object for each level 0 placement that shows a model. The expected counts come from the RuneLite reference files of the landscape and of the loc definitions.
- [x] Placements with the same loc model, recolours and retextures share one mesh. A contoured placement on flat ground shares, and on uneven ground it has its own mesh, as ADR 0022 and ADR 0023 say.
- [x] Impostor and animated locs show as the spec says.
- [x] The import still ends in one undo step.
- [x] The pull request states the run time of the import.
- [x] `prek run --all-files` passes and the pyrefly baseline has no new entry.

## Verification

```bash
RSPS_SNAPSHOT_430_CACHE=<path to cache> BLENDER_USER_RESOURCES="$PWD/.blender-test-profile" scripts/test-blender.sh tests/blender/test_region_import.py
prek run --all-files
```

Follow the Boundaries of the spec. Report each guess and each choice that the spec does not decide.

parent.title: Import a map chunk (terrain and scenery) into Blender
parent.body:
As an engineer, I want to import a chunk of the game map (e.g. Draynor Village) into Blender, with its terrain and the scenery on it, so that a player built with the add-on can stand in a real area instead of an empty scene.

Right now the add-on only handles models. `formats/js5.py` says encrypted groups (map landscapes) are not supported, and `docs/osrs-cache-workflow.md` notes that 268 landscapes in snapshot 430 have no exported key.

The first use for this is a 3D scene on my profile page, exported from Blender as glTF. I think the import should land here first, and the export side can be adjusted for the page after.

Not settled yet:

- Which cache archives hold the terrain and the landscape (scenery placement) of a region, and which keys the landscapes need.
- How much to import at once: one region, a rectangle of tiles, or a named area.
- Whether scenery objects (trees, walls, buildings) come in with the terrain, or in a later step.
- How the tile colors, overlays and textures become Blender materials.
- Whether the result needs to export to glTF with the same look.
